paragraphs.text: Dear sisters and elders, by now you should all know that we are in the lockdown until at least May 15th. It may go longer, but let's hope and pray that we get some more flexibility soon.

I'm grateful you all have your 14-day supply of food and water. That helps us all have a little bit more peace of mind and frankly a little more sense of security as we go into these uncertain circumstances that we're facing.
One thing I learned in my life is that even in the face of unpleasant circumstances it is best to keep a positive outlook. It seems the brain and the heart all do better when a person stays positive.

When I get out of bed in the morning I have learned to say out loud, quote, "it's going to be a great day today," close quote. I say this no matter what the day looks like or how I might feel at the time.

This idea was reinforced for me many years ago by Elder F. Enzio Busche. He was a member of the Seventy a long, long time ago and he once said this in a talk to BYU students, quote, "embrace this day with an enthusiastic welcome no matter how it looks. The covenant with God to which you are and true enables you to become enlightened by Him and nothing is impossible for you," close quote.

Thinking like that just changes your outlook on the day. It changes your outlook on life and it spurs and increases creativity in you to start looking for evidence that justifies the position that you're taking and automatically you start seeing good things that were always there but you didn't see before because in your negative frame of mind you were looking for evidence to justify your negative frame of mind.

So by switching to a positive frame of mind you literally see things here again that were always there but that you didn't see and those positive things reinforce your feeling that things are going to be alright. In fact they're going to be great.

So by getting out of bed and first thing saying out loud today is going to be a great day. I am greeting this day with an enthusiastic welcome. Truly life is good and God is great so let's go forward in faith and find joy in service. It's really our choice. I think that's what we're learning.
Okay let's finish up this series on the five smooth stones with our talk on smooth stone number five which is renewal.
Abraham Lincoln a great American president once said quote, "give me six hours to chop down a tree and I will spend the first four hours sharpening the axe." Close quote.
What Lincoln is trying to teach us here is that we've got to renew ourselves so that our optimal self will be doing the work when the work needs to get done.

I have watched friends of mine on Wall Street and in other high powered occupations become very good at the first four smooth stones but then they have a complete mental breakdown or emotional meltdown or a collapse of some kind because they burned themselves out.

Human beings are not machines and we can't operate like machines very long before we do serious damage to ourselves. Even machines need maintenance or they break down and we understand that reality with machines but we many times forget that a human being is much more delicate, much more complicated than a machine and it ourselves the human body requires maintenance on a regular basis and what I call maintenance with machines I call renewal with the human body and mind.

Renewal is an essential element in high achievement. The person who doesn't take the time to renew both body and spirit will see a gradual decline or erosion of competence and productivity and if that doesn't wake that person up to his dangerous path downhill then he will eventually just collapse or burn out.

I've always loved the line in Ernest Hemingway's masterpiece The Sun Also Rises when one person in the book asks another how did you go bankrupt? The second person answers two ways, first gradually and then suddenly. How does a person burn out? Two ways, first gradually and then suddenly.

Smooth Stone 5 prevents both ways from happening. By having a regular and consistent process of renewal a person not only fortifies themselves from burnout but also elevates their thinking to a whole new level.

I was born in Utah, a part of the United States that's right in the middle of the Rocky Mountains. I grew up in the mountains and have learned most of what I know that's really important in the mountains.

One of my favorite hobbies is high altitude climbing. I've climbed big mountains all over the world. It's a fun hobby but it is far more important to me than just being a hobby. It is where I obtain renewal.

I have not only renewed my spirit in the mountains, I've also greatly increased my physical, emotional and mental strength in the mountains. I've had some of my most important ideas and breakthroughs in the mountains.

People have asked me how can you justify spending six weeks climbing a mountain when you have this big business with all its demands and these people depending upon you? The answer is that first you put processes into place. You build systems from the processes and then you put people in place and have them learn the systems and you make sure they can follow the system well enough to create the quality that is necessary.
Then you get out of there and you get into some place. For me it was into the mountains where you can think about what you should do next. That's renewal.

Some people find renewal at the beach. Some people find it in the forest. Other people find it through exercise. Others find it through reading a good book. There are a million plus ways to find renewal. The key is that you find a way that works for you.
Now I haven't been able to go to the mountains during this three-year mission that I accepted but the mission itself can be a powerful opportunity to renew for the next part of my life.

In the mission, however, I also need ways to renew my body and mind and spirit from the work of the mission, the stress of the mission. And I've found that getting outside for some healthy sunshine in the early morning is one way that I enjoy, even during the lockdown.

Writing kind emails to people that have blessed my life in the past is another way that I find renewal during the lockdown. There are always actions you can take that will bring renewal to you. Some of the best are meditation and prayer. And you can do them wherever you are.

I'm grateful to be here and to experience this renewal and growth that comes from serving the Lord as a full-time missionary but also comes from those interludes of renewal within the mission that brings a heightened desire and ability to serve ever better and more competently and wisely.

Those have been blessings for me and I'm sure they've been blessings for you as I've heard from many of you and other missionaries who have already completed their mission that it was during their mission that they learned some of the things that they learned that will bless them for the rest of their lives.

So there you have the very shortened presentation on my five smooth stones. Smooth stone number one, vision and goals. Smooth stone number two, schedule priorities, get the one percent in your life. Three, processes and systems. Four, measurement and accountability. And five, renewal.

I hope you can use these smooth stones yourself to get great effects in your life. I promise you that if you do, if you really put in the energy and the time, you can make them yours so that they're not mine but yours.

And when they're yours, you can use them to grow yourself and do far better than I've done in my life because you're learning them when you're younger. That's a powerful blessing that you have if you take advantage of it, if you choose.

Our next series of audio messages are going to be about one of two things. Whether how to be more happy or how to change our lives through losing bad habits and making good ones. Why don't you give me your opinion on which I should choose? Send me a message over the next day or two on your preferred topic and then I'll start that series on Monday.
Again, I want to remind you that Sister Hughes and I love you very much. We are so grateful to serve with you at this historic time.

Never again, probably in our lifetimes, certainly never in our lifetimes to this point, have we ever seen anything like what we're seeing in the world today. And we actually get the blessing and benefit of serving a full-time mission right in the middle of it. Pretty amazing. God bless you all. We'll talk to you soon.
